about: Frontier-written worked examples for the CI-1 compose path (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-10-22). Generic first-party automations, written before any builder call and NOT derived from any bed item: they show the IR mechanics (input, code node, map over a planned list, conditional post, keyed sheet writes, webhook answer). Frozen by hash in research/ci1-20261021/MANIFEST.json.

examples.request: Every weekday at 8am, e-mail each task owner the tasks they own that are overdue (due date before today, status not done in any capitalisation), one e-mail per owner listing title and due date. If anything is overdue, post the count to #team. Then set reminded_on to today's date on those tasks.

tasks.about: task_id is unique; due is YYYY-MM-DD

workflow.title: Overdue task reminders
workflow.goal: Remind each owner of their overdue tasks, tell #team how many, and record the reminder date.

successCriteria: One e-mail per owner with overdue tasks

nodes.description: Find overdue tasks, group them by owner, write the texts and the sheet updates

examples.request: Our signup form posts name and email to a webhook and waits for a JSON answer. Trim both and lowercase the e-mail. Without a valid e-mail answer {"ok": false, "error": "invalid email"} with status 400 and do nothing else. Otherwise keep one row per e-mail in contacts: add new people with visits 1, and for someone already there update their name and add 1 to visits; then answer {"ok": true}.

trigger.payload: event.body has name and email (either may be missing)

workflow.title: Signup webhook
workflow.goal: Validate a signup, keep one contact row per e-mail with a visit count, and answer the form.

nodes.description: Validate and decide the write and the answer
